name: T-6 Texan II
summary: Single-turboprop primary trainer, derived from the Pilatus PC-9, used for the first stage of USAF, Navy and Marine Corps pilot training.

wings: Low-mounted straight tapered wing with dihedral
engines: Single turboprop driving a four-blade propeller
Exhaust stacks on both sides of the long nose
fuselage: Tandem two-seat cockpit under a long bubble canopy, rear seat raised
Slim fuselage, usually white with blue (USAF) or white/orange (Navy) trim
tail: Single vertical fin with a dorsal fillet sweeping forward along the spine
Small ventral strake under the tail

tellTales: Single turboprop with tandem seats under a bubble canopy
Long nose with exhaust stacks on each side
Dorsal fin fillet sweeping forward from the tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The T-6 is larger with a four-blade prop, a raised rear seat under a one-piece bubble canopy and a dorsal fin fillet; the T-34 is smaller with a framed sliding canopy.
The T-6 has a slim turboprop nose with side exhaust stacks; the T-28 has a big round radial-engine cowling.
The Tucano has a shorter nose and a lower, longer canopy; the T-6 Texan II has a taller canopy hump and a longer nose.
The PC-7 has a three-blade propeller, a smaller airframe and a lower canopy; the T-6 Texan II has a four-blade propeller and a bigger airframe.
The PC-9 is the smaller, sleeker airplane the T-6 Texan II was derived from, with a lower canopy and a smaller tail; the T-6 is larger and heavier-looking.
